knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The learner cleans their own hands and reports the touch point so the facility can respond. Ignoring it, touching the surface bare-handed or confronting the visitor each fails the procedure.
A tissue or the crook of the arm keeps droplets off the hands. The palm, uniform, sleeve and turn-away options all move droplets onto surfaces or clothing.
Hand cleaning follows contact with respiratory secretions even when a bin was used. The other options skip hand cleaning or add a hazardous step.

practicalCriteria: During a walk-through of a waiting area, the learner states the cough steps in order and names the bin used for tissues.
The learner demonstrates the report to a supervisor using a sample touch point and time.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Sample shift record entry showing a correct report
stopWorkCriteria: A person with symptoms is in a care area and no supervisor is available to decide the next step
Tissues or hand cleaning products are missing and the area is in use
